verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug ... likely present in every release from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). Dan found and fixed it on 2026-03-03
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed...' 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09)... fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)... Backports... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'

verdicts.claim: NOOP mode copies no frames... SQLite added it in 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) as PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(NOOP) and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP
verdicts.evidence: 3.51.3 release log, under 'Prior changes from version 3.51.0 (2025-11-04)': 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument'

verdicts.claim: The default page size was almost always 1024 bytes before SQLite 3.12.0 (2016-03-29) and is 4096 bytes since
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'the default page size was almost always 1024 bytes, but beginning with SQLite version 3.12.0 (2016-03-29), the default page size increased to 4096'

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x ... truncate-page-n, defaults to 121359 pages (about 500 MB). Since v0.5.15 it tries PASSIVE first ... min-checkpoint-page-count cannot be 0
verdicts.evidence: guide: 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB'; 'v0.5.15 ... Litestream first attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint'; 'checkpoint-interval: 1m'; 'min-checkpoint-page-count option cannot be set to 0'

verdicts.claim: Antithesis (2026-08-12) caught the bug on 3.51.2 in about 15 minutes of its first run, using a generic workload
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis: 'On my first run, Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins'; 'repeated the exercise with 3.51.3 ... the run came back green'

verdicts.claim: Phil Eaton (2026-08-23) reproduced the bug with about 100 lines of C ... within about 3.5 to 4.3 seconds per run. A 3.53.0 build lost nothing in ~16 s
verdicts.evidence: Eaton: 'About 100 lines of C', 'two threads and three database connections', runs real 0m4.286s / 0m3.454s, 3.53.0 run real 0m15.946s 'permanently lost: 0'; wal.html 'UPDATE: 2026-08-24 → Phil Eaton has devised a reproducer'

verdicts.claim: A manual PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(RESTART) ... can return SQLITE_BUSY in about a microsecond ... 2021 forum case (36 connections, about 1000 writes per second)
verdicts.evidence: forum: '36 connections ... about 1000 writes per second', 'busy_timeout of 10 seconds', 'returns busy within a microsecond'; fix 'Setting PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; on every connection resolves the issue'

verdicts.claim: Techzine reports nineteen database corruption incidents over about half a year in a control plane where Tailscale triggers checkpoints itself
verdicts.evidence: Techzine: 'nineteen instances of database corruption over the course of half a year'; Register quote: 'running at our own aggressive pace, we stepped off the well-trodden operational path'

verdicts.claim: SQLite withdrew 3.52.0 after Tailscale reported corruption in thirteen databases. Techzine calls that report a false alarm: floating-point rounding
verdicts.evidence: Techzine: 'Tailscale reported corruption in thirteen databases. This turned out to be a false alarm ... altered the rounding of certain floating-point conversions ... SQLite withdrew version 3.52.0'

verdicts.claim: In the Syncthing thread of 2026-02-06, the maintainer named three causes ... transactions open for hours, such as vacuum; ... connection pool
verdicts.evidence: thread dated 'February 6, 2026': 'If a transaction is open for hours ... vacuum handling'; 'move the logic into our connection pool'; 'critical levels of multiple gigabytes'; 'the WAL will grow indefinitely until we're able to complete a checkpoint'

notes: All 14 reference URLs were in the source cache with text; zero web fetches used.
Syncthing poster is described as 'the maintainer'; the cached text does not show a role label, so that attribution was not independently confirmed (substance supported).
No reviewer-addressed instructions found in sampled sources.
